raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran the changed-file pre-commit hooks and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable Hard Rules in the repository and test AGENTS.md files.
- [ ] I added the required labels. The contributor account cannot apply upstream labels; requested: `cat-bugfix`, `area:sparse_attention`, `op:DSA`, `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

SM90 dense score recomputation runs two consumer warp groups and a producer down separate control-flow branches. Their named barriers currently lower to aligned `bar.sync` / `bar.arrive` despite the warp-role split; synccheck reports divergent threads and terminates the instrumented launch. Racecheck also reports shared-memory hazards between the initial weights fill and producer writes, between reduction reads and slot reuse, and between a consumer's weight/LSE read and the next head tile's producer writes.

Use non-aligned CTA sync and arrive operations while retaining the existing barrier IDs, participant counts and ping-pong schedule. Initialize weights before the initial CTA barrier, protect each consumer's reduction reads before the slots are reused, and add a cross-group handoff when more than one head tile reuses weights/LSE. Add numerical and sanitizer regressions for both score types and both producer modes.

## Related work

Related to #2252, which addresses the separately launched SM90 sparse score kernel. #2244 addresses an independent SM100-family dense score publication path.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API changes. The change targets SM90. The CUDA 12 CuTe DSL compiler runs used the CUDA 13 PyTorch/cuDNN runtime; they are not end-to-end CUDA 12 deployment tests.

## Testing

- GH200 (SM90), develop `f88a1ef2`, cuDNN 9.27.0.42, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, DSL 4.8.1/cu13: two selected sanitizer regressions fail on the base (synccheck attention and racecheck indexer); with this change `test_DSA_dense_score_sync_sm90.py`: **12 passed**, covering attention/indexer, unified/split producer, normal execution, synccheck and racecheck.
- With this change, the two original single-shape repros each passed normal execution, memcheck, synccheck and racecheck. The prior multi-head candidate still triggered two racecheck failures; the final cross-group weight/LSE handoff removes those failures in the 12-test run.
- Existing SM90 dense attention and indexer boundary tests: **20 passed, 39 deselected**, including multi-head and THD-wrapper cases.
- Cold-compile BF16 reference checks: four cases each with DSL 4.8.0/cu12, 4.8.0/cu13 and 4.8.1/cu12: **12 passed**. DSL 4.8.1/cu13 is covered by the regression and existing tests. The loaded DSL compiler versions were CUDA 12.9 and 13.4 respectively.
- CUDA Graph replays for both score paths and both producer modes matched references after changing Q and weights/LSE.
- PTX inspection shows the role-scoped named sync/arrive instructions use `barrier.sync` / `barrier.arrive`; the unconditional initial CTA barrier remains `bar.sync`.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

The tested shapes do not constitute full SM90 performance qualification. For one warmed CUDA Graph replay shape, attention medians were 8.86/8.90 us (base) and 8.74/8.80 us (fix); indexer medians were 6.94/7.07 us (base) and 7.05/6.94 us (fix). These short measurements are not a general performance claim.

Offline compilation does not establish runtime correctness or qualify the author's compiler matrix. Current-head workflows require approval. No workflow approval or alternate CI trigger was sent. +# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""SM90 dense score warp-role synchronization and shared-memory reuse."""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from deepseek_sparse_attention.cutedsl import test_DSA_dense_score_recompute as dense_tests
+
+
+def _require_sm90():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (9, 0):
+        pytest.skip("requires SM90")
+
+
+_CASES = [
+    pytest.param("attention", 0, id="attention-unified"),
+    pytest.param("attention", 1, id="attention-split"),
+    pytest.param("indexer", 0, id="indexer-unified"),
+    pytest.param("indexer", 1, id="indexer-split"),
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score_type,split_producer", _CASES)
+def test_dense_sm90_sync_reference(monkeypatch, score_type, split_producer):
+    _require_sm90()
+    from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.score_recompute import _interface_sm90
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("DENSE3WG_USE_WARP_SPLIT_PROD", str(split_producer))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(_interface_sm90._dense_score_recompute, "compile_cache", {})
+    if score_type == "attention":
+        # H128 uses two head tiles; the test includes wholly masked rows and a KV tail.
+        dense_tests.test_DSA_dense_attn_sm90_masked_output(heads=128, ratio=1, is_thd=False)
+    else:
+        # Exercise singleton, short and partial KV shapes through the same cache.
+        dense_tests.test_DSA_dense_indexer_sm90_singleton_and_mask_cache(heads=32, ratio=1, singleton_first=True, monkeypatch=monkeypatch)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@pytest.mark.gpu_exclusive
+@pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="gpu_exclusive")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score_type,split_producer", _CASES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", ["synccheck", "racecheck"])
+def test_dense_sm90_sync_sanitizer(score_type, split_producer, tool):
+    _require_sm90()
+    toolkit_sanitizer = Path(os.environ.get("CUDA_HOME", "/usr/local/cuda")) / "bin" / "compute-sanitizer"
+    sanitizer = str(toolkit_sanitizer) if toolkit_sanitizer.is_file() and os.access(toolkit_sanitizer, os.X_OK) else shutil.which("compute-sanitizer")
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        sanitizer = next((str(p) for p in sorted(Path("/usr/local").glob("cuda*/bin/compute-sanitizer"))), None)
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        return pytest.skip("compute-sanitizer is not installed")
+    case = f"{score_type}-{'split' if split_producer else 'unified'}"
+    test_timeout = float(os.environ.get("CUDNN_TEST_TIMEOUT", "1500"))
+    timeout = min(300.0, 0.6 * test_timeout) if test_timeout > 0 else 300.0
+    child = f"import faulthandler,sys; faulthandler.dump_traceback_later({timeout * 0.9!r}); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(sys.argv[1:]))"
+    cmd = [
+        sanitizer,
+        "--tool",
+        tool,
+        "--report-api-errors",
+        "no",
+        "--error-exitcode",
+        "9",
+        "--print-limit",
+        "10",
+        sys.executable,
+        "-u",
+        "-c",
+        child,
+        f"{Path(__file__).resolve()}::test_dense_sm90_sync_reference[{case}]",
+        "-n0",
+        "-o",
+        "addopts=",
+        "-p",
+        "no:cacheprovider",
+        "-q",
+    ]
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, start_new_session=True)
+    try:
+        out, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
+        os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        rest, _ = proc.communicate()
+        prior = exc.output.decode(errors="replace") if isinstance(exc.output, bytes) else (exc.output or "")
+        raise AssertionError(f"{tool} timed out after {timeout}s\n{prior}{rest}") from None
+    assert proc.returncode == 0, out[-8000:]
+    assert "1 passed" in out, out[-8000:]
+    if tool == "synccheck":
+        assert "ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors" in out, out[-8000:]
+    else:
+        assert "0 errors, 0 warnings" in out, out[-8000:]

Existing labels are preserved; milestone and project membership are set.

Offline compilation does not establish runtime correctness or qualify the author's compiler matrix. Current-head workflows require approval. No workflow approval or alternate CI trigger was sent.
